name: Set up a fish tank properly
blurb: The reason beginner fish die is almost always the nitrogen cycle. Cycling a tank before adding fish takes a month of patience and prevents nearly every common disaster.
gear: The largest tank you have room for — small tanks are harder, not easier
Filter, heater, test kit for ammonia, nitrite and nitrate
A source of ammonia for a fishless cycle
steps: Learn the nitrogen cycle: fish waste becomes ammonia, bacteria convert it to nitrite, then to less harmful nitrate, which water changes remove.
Cycle the tank without fish: add an ammonia source and test until ammonia and nitrite both read zero within 24 hours. This takes four to eight weeks.
Research stocking properly before buying anything — adult size, temperament and water parameters. Most beginner mistakes are bought in a shop in ten minutes.
Add fish slowly, a few at a time, so the bacteria colony can keep up.
Establish a weekly routine of partial water changes and gravel cleaning, with dechlorinated water at matched temperature.
Test regularly and quarantine new fish before adding them to an established tank.
tips: Goldfish need far more space than a bowl; a bowl is not a suitable home for any fish.
Never clean the filter media in tap water — chlorine kills the bacteria and crashes the cycle.
proof: A stable tank running six months with zero ammonia and nitrite, and healthy fish.
